claim: Optimizing a small set of LoRA adapters on a few layers (SafeReAct) can reactivate a post-trained LLM's original safety mechanisms, improving safety on harmful prompts without degrading domain-specific performance.
falsifier: On a post-trained LLM with degraded safety, apply SafeReAct by training LoRA adapters on a few layers using harmful prompts and the model's own safety-related representations; measure safety improvement on harmful prompts and verify no degradation on domain-specific tasks.

conditions: The model has undergone post-training that masks safety mechanisms
The intervention uses a lightweight LoRA-based alignment on a small number of layers
Evaluation includes both harmful prompts and domain-specific benchmarks
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported models (R1-7B, R1-8B, R1-14B, R1-32B, QwQ-8B, QwQ-32B, medical and financial LLMs) and the specific SafeReAct implementation; transfer to other architectures or training setups is unestablished.

title: Optimization of LoRA adapters for Restoration of safe behavior

claim: Hierarchical context engineering provides the largest gains when reasoning depth is limited or when the candidate set cannot be exhaustively ranked by a single agent.
falsifier: The claim can be tested by comparing hierarchical and single-agent performance across tasks with varying reasoning depth and candidate set size.

conditions: Candidate set cannot be exhaustively ranked by a single agent
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the two chemical domains studied and the specific hierarchical architectures; transfer to other domains or architectures is unestablished.

title: Hierarchical context engineering–Search efficiency gain over boundary

claim: For a process with problem size given by number of edges e, the depth is O(e) and the required qubit number is O(e + n), where n is the number of vertices.
falsifier: The scaling can be verified by implementing the process for graphs with varying e and n.

conditions: Problem size is taken as the number of edges e
exclusions: Limited to the described process and its formal analysis

title: A graph-based process–Circuit depth and required theorem
